note.after_visit_summary: You came in about a mole on your upper back near your shoulder blade. We looked at it closely and it looks different from your other moles, so we could not tell just by looking whether it is benign or something more serious. Because it is changing, we did a quick shave biopsy today to take a sample to the lab. This will not need stitches. Keep the bandage on for 24 hours. After that, wash the area gently once a day, put on plain petroleum jelly, and cover it with a fresh bandage every day until it heals, usually in 1 to 2 weeks. Call us if the area becomes red, hot, swollen, or starts draining pus. Your results should be ready in 7 to 10 days and will appear in your patient portal; someone will also call you either way. We will review the results together at your follow-up on Tuesday, October 27th. For now, wear sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher every day on exposed skin and reapply every 2 hours when outside. Wear a wide-brimmed hat. Check your moles once a month. Because you have had blistering sunburns and several moles, you will need a full skin check every year.
